newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Primark, Dow Jones news deal.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Primark, Dow Jones news deal.

text.p: Primark Corp and Dow Jones & Co said on Thursday that they have started a joint venture equities news information service in the United Kingdom and Ireland, to be launched in the first half of 1997.
The following is a full text of their news release.

WALTHAM, Mass., Oct. 24 /PRNewswire/ -- Primark Corporation (NYSE/PSE: PMK) and Dow Jones & Company (NYSE: DJ) today announced a joint venture to develop a comprehensive real-time financial information product for equity traders and investors to be offered initially in the United Kingdom and Ireland. The new product, called the Primark/Dow Jones Equities Service, will also become Dow Jones Telerate's equities product in these countries. It is scheduled for release in the first half of 1997.

Integrated with expanded Dow Jones news and the news services produced through Dow Jones' partnership with the Associated Press, the new product will deliver global financial data including quotes, earnings estimates, and historical economic and financial information to equity traders and investors. The information will be available through workstations, digital data feeds and trading room systems, including those of Dow Jones Telerate. The Primark/Dow Jones Equities Service will provide news coverage and equity market information from exchanges and companies around the world.
Primark and Dow Jones said future plans call for tailoring the product for distribution in continental Europe and to other parts of the world.

In a related announcement (see additional release), Primark acquired UK- based ICV, Limited, the leading provider of real-time UK equity data and a highly regarded source of real-time news in the UK market. Primark's acquisition of ICV, and ICV's capabilities, will be key elements in developing the Primark/Dow Jones Equities Service. Primark will be responsible for all marketing, sales and customer support of the product, working closely with the Dow Jones Telerate and the AP-Dow Jones marketing staffs.

The Primark/Dow Jones joint venture will combine key information services and management resources from each company. Both parties plan to make substantial investments to develop and sell the service. Terms of the agreement, which is subject to a definitive contract and certain regulatory approvals, were not disclosed.

"The joint venture between Primark and Dow Jones combines two companies that have the best news, quotes and information services from the best industry sources. When combined with ICV's proven ability in the real-time data business and other existing information companies within the Primark group, we have created a "Dream Team" of information sources that will be better than any product existing today," said Joseph E. Kasputys, chairman and chief executive officer of Primark Corporation. "The joint venture between Primark and Dow Jones is in response to the tremendous need we've seen from international equity traders and investors for the real-time delivery of quality financial information and news through the technology and delivery systems that best suit their needs."

Kenneth L. Burenga, president of Dow Jones and chief executive officer of Dow Jones Telerate, said, "Increasingly, customers are looking to Dow Jones Telerate as a full-service provider to meet all of their business news, financial data, and decision-support needs. This joint venture with Primark significantly enhances Dow Jones' ability to satisfy customers, regardless of whether their businesses are in equities, fixed-income, foreign exchange, commodities or related markets."

Primark Corporation, headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, is a $600 million global provider of information technology solutions, combining highly advanced software and applications with some of the most accurate, timely and comprehensive databases in the world. The company, through its subsidiaries, targets the data intensive financial, government, weather and communications/computer information markets. Primark's financial information businesses, including Datastream, Disclosure and I/B/E/S, are leaders in providing global financial information markets with historical, economic, and financial information and analysis. TASC, the company's information technology unit, has the capabilities to develop high-end complex information systems to manage and deliver comprehensive information through state-of-the- art technology to customers.

Dow Jones & Company, Inc. is the parent company of Dow Jones Telerate, a leading global provider of news and market information, real-time prices, decision-support products, trading room systems and transaction services for financial institutions.

Dow Jones also publishes The Wall Street Journal and its international editions, The Wall Street Journal Interactive Edition, Barron's magazine and other periodicals, electronic business information services and the Ottaway group of community newspapers.

Electronic information services include the Dow Jones News Service, the AP-Dow Jones news services joint venture, and other business newswires; and Business Information Services, which provides business news and information products, including The Wall Street Journal Interactive Edition on the World Wide Web and Dow Jones News/Retrieval, to corporations, consumers and private investors through a variety of media: computer, telephone, facsimile and radio. Dow Jones also produces business television programming inally.
